column1: # CC-EN-VARIANTS F1: accepted spelling variants for English. stored<TAB>accepted<TAB>source<TAB>kind
# stored = the US form; accepted = the British/Commonwealth form. Read by src/accepted.rs; the grader reads accepted variants from nowhere else.
# English is graded BOTH WAYS (Eric, 2026-10-19: either spelling is right, whichever the bank stores) -- unlike de/ja, which are one-way. The Settings
# British switch (variants.rs) shows `accepted` when on and `stored` when off.
# A variant is a spelling of the SAME word, never a near-sound. No pair is generated from a pattern. `kind` is a label, not a rule.
# source: eric-2026-10-19 = the list Eric signed on that date (hand-written, migrated unchanged from assets/words/en/spelling-variants.tsv, 209 pairs).
# Added 2026-11-04 on Eric's ruling (identical audio: rejecting one spelling makes the prompt unanswerable). SCOWL en_US-large lists both spellings.
# F4 diacritic loanwords (Eric 2026-11-04): the bank stores the plain form, the accented one is accepted, never required. SCOWL en_US-large lists both. No accent keys are added for English.
